children.author: perpetuallunch

children.author: esskay
children.textRawHtml:
South Australia is a good example. In 2023–24, wind supplied 45.2% of South Australia’s electricity generation, rooftop solar supplied 18.3%, and large-scale solar another 10.7%. In other words, roughly 74% of the state’s electricity generation came from wind and solar. [1]

And this isn’t a comparison that ignores inflation. AEMO publishes its historical wholesale electricity prices in real June 2024 dollars. South Australia’s average wholesale price in 2023–24 was A$79.53/MWh, compared with roughly A$95/MWh in 2012–13. It was also 40% lower than the previous year’s A$131.90/MWh. [1]

AEMO also specifically identifies increased rooftop and grid-scale solar output as one of the factors contributing to lower wholesale prices. [1]

So there’s a fairly straightforward example: South Australia reached roughly 74% wind and solar generation while its inflation-adjusted wholesale electricity price was lower than it had been around a decade earlier.

That obviously doesn’t mean renewables were the only factor affecting prices - electricity markets are influenced by fuel prices, interconnectors, demand, storage and plenty of other things. But it does disprove the claim that high penetration of wind and solar necessarily results in higher inflation-adjusted electricity prices.

[1] https://www.aemo.com.au/-/media/files/electricity/nem/planni...

I'm sure this wont be enough or acceptable though will it. It never is.
children.textZhHtml:
南澳大利亚就是一个很好的例子。 2023-24 年，风力发电占南澳大利亚发电量的 45.2%，屋顶太阳能发电量占 18.3%，大型太阳能发电量占 10.7%。换句话说，该州大约 74% 的发电量来自风能和太阳能。 [1]

这并不是一个忽略通货膨胀的比较。 AEMO 以 2024 年 6 月实际美元价格公布其历史批发电价。南澳大利亚州 2023-24 年的平均批发价格为 79.53 澳元/兆瓦时，而 2012-13 年约为 95 澳元/兆瓦时。也比去年的 131.90 澳元/兆瓦时低 40%。 [1]

AEMO 还特别指出屋顶和电网规模太阳能输出的增加是导致批发价格下降的因素之一。 [1]

因此，有一个相当简单的例子：南澳大利亚州的风能和太阳能发电量达到了约 74%，而其经通胀调整的批发电价低于十年前左右。

这显然并不意味着可再生能源是影响价格的唯一因素 - 电力市场受到燃料价格、互连器、需求、存储和许多其他因素的影响。但它确实反驳了风能和太阳能的高普及率必然会导致通货膨胀调整后的电价上涨的说法。

[1] https://www.aemo.com.au/-/media/files/electricity/nem/planni...

stories.title: What happens if an entire class of workers loses faith in their careers
stories.titleZh: 如果整个阶层的工人对自己的职业失去信心会发生什么

comments.author: Animats
comments.textRawHtml:
Addressing the question in the title, "What happens if an entire class of workers loses faith in their careers", look at what happened to printers. That was a good skilled trade for centuries. Then it just went away. Phototypesetting took the high volume end. Desktop publishing took the low end. Computer-controlled presses took press operators. And then the newspaper business died.

I've heard homeless former printers talking about the good days at the Burger King near the cable car turntable at Powell and Market. They thought they had careers. Now they're struggling to survive.

Knitting is not the answer. This is a survival issue. Somehow I suspect the author inherited money.
comments.textZhHtml:
解决标题中的问题“如果整个阶级的工人对自己的职业失去信心会发生什么”，看看打印机发生了什么。几个世纪以来，这一直是一项良好的熟练贸易。然后它就消失了。照相排版占据了高产量。桌面出版占据了低端市场。计算机控制的印刷机取代了印刷机操作员。然后报纸生意就消亡了。

我听到无家可归的前印刷商谈论在鲍威尔和市场缆车转盘附近的汉堡王的美好时光。他们以为自己有事业。 现在他们正在为生存而挣扎。

编织不是答案。这是一个生存问题。不知怎的，我怀疑作者继承了钱。

children.author: estearum
children.textRawHtml:
Surprised no one has made the extremely obvious observation that it took literal centuries for printing technology to eliminate the trade of printers, which could not have possibly have employed more than 0.01% of people at its peak.

Compared to the potential obsolescence of 40% to 60% of the US workforce over the course of 10 - 20 years?

You can argue about whether the obsolescence is real or not, but if it is, the plight of the printers is totally incomparable.

Question: What happens when you drive a car at 90 mph into a concrete wall?

Answer: Well, actually just this morning pulling into my parking spot, I bumped into the barrier beneath my tires. It was fine!
children.textZhHtml:
令人惊讶的是，没有人做出极其明显的观察，即印刷技术花了几个世纪的时间才消除了打印机贸易，而打印机在其巅峰时期雇用的人口不可能超过 0.01%。

与 10 - 20 年间美国劳动力 40% 到 60% 的潜在淘汰相比？

你可以争论这种淘汰是真实的还是不是，但是如果是，打印机的困境是完全无法比拟的。

问题：当你以 90 英里/小时的速度驾驶汽车撞上混凝土墙时会发生什么？

答案：嗯，实际上就在今天早上，我把车开进停车位时，就撞到了轮胎下面的护栏上。很好！

children.author: thegrim33
children.textRawHtml: The difference is that one of those things actually happened, and the other one is your hypothetical extremist/exaggerated/worst possible case of what might happen this time.
children.textZhHtml: 区别在于，其中一件事确实发生了，另一件事是您假设的极端/夸张/最糟糕的情况，这一次可能会发生。

children.author: estearum
children.textRawHtml: the wise man bowed his head solemnly and spoke: "theres actually zero reason to think about events that haven't happened yet. you imbecile. you fucking moron"
children.textZhHtml: 智者郑重地低下了头，说道：“其实没有理由去思考尚未发生的事情。你这个白痴。你他妈的白痴”

children.author: altmanaltman
children.textRawHtml: Yeah + the world was much different than it is today. It trivializes the risk by saying we have seen it before and we were okay when its a fundamentally different problem in many aspects.
children.textZhHtml: 是的，当时的世界与今天有很大不同。它轻视了风险，说我们以前见过这种情况，而且我们没问题，但实际上它在很多方面都是一个根本不同的问题。

children.author: Macha
children.textRawHtml: Also fails to distinguish between “society came out of it fine” (generally true) and “individuals came out of it fine” (much more mixed of a track record)
children.textZhHtml: 也无法区分“社会一切顺利”（通常是正确的）和“个人一切顺利”（业绩记录更加复杂）

children.author: rayiner
children.textRawHtml: Yes. And individuals largely don’t come out fine. We have this notion of “retraining” but that’s not real. It’s like how studies show it’s very hard to make friends as an adult. Most people whose jobs were shipped overseas in deindustrialization never recovers.
children.textZhHtml: 是的。个人基本上都不会好起来。我们有“再培训”的概念，但这不是真实的。就像研究表明成年人很难交朋友一样。大多数在去工业化过程中工作被转移到海外的人永远无法恢复。

children.author: lesuorac
children.textRawHtml:
> We have this notion of “retraining” but that’s not real.

While I haven't been "retrained" my understanding was the real issue that it's lip-service.

Like the Department of Labor doesn't actually show up to a closed down factory with staff to train people in some other vocation.
children.textZhHtml:
> 我们有“再培训”的概念，但这不是真实的。

虽然我没有接受过“再培训”，但我的理解是真正的问题是它只是口头上的。

就像劳工部实际上并没有带着员工出现在一家关闭的工厂来培训其他职业的人员一样。

children.author: logicchains
children.textRawHtml: University-educated "Knowledge workers" should be much more capable of learning new things than the average factory production line worker.
children.textZhHtml: 受过大学教育的“知识工人”应该比普通工厂生产线工人更有能力学习新事物。

children.author: chongli
children.textRawHtml:
How is the GGP post (by Animats) trivializing the risk? They're saying "it's a survival issue" and saying the printers became homeless and struggling to feed themselves.

Sounds much more like a warning than a dismissal to me. If 40-50% of the workforce ends up like that then we're living in a post-apocalyptic wasteland failed state.
children.textZhHtml:
GGP 帖子（Animats 发布）是如何淡化风险的？他们说“这是一个生存问题”，并说印刷商无家可归，难以养活自己。

对我来说，这听起来更像是警告，而不是解雇。如果 40-50% 的劳动力最终变成这样，那么我们就生活在一个后世界末日的荒地失败状态。

children.author: rayiner
children.textRawHtml:
> If 40-50% of the workforce ends up like that then we're living in a post-apocalyptic wasteland failed state.

I a lot less than that. Most people don’t have jobs that can be done remotely, which I think is a good proxy for the ceiling of who can be replaced by AI. Almost nobody on my block besides me is going to be replaced (beer brewer, several nurses, navy servicemen, cops, and teachers).
children.textZhHtml:
> 如果 40-50% 的劳动力最终都是这样，那么我们就生活在一个后世界末日的荒地失败状态。

我比这要少得多。大多数人没有可以远程完成的工作，我认为这很好地体现了人工智能可以取代谁的上限。除了我之外，我所在街区几乎没有人会被取代（啤酒酿造商、几名护士、海军军人、警察和教师）。

children.author: Recurecur
children.textRawHtml:
I think you’re failing to factor in the rapid improvement in robotics.

I was at the hospital a few days ago, and was pondering the numerous nurses who were wheeling around portable nursing stations with monitors and various types of equipment. They’d stop at a room, take a patient’s blood pressure (among various other things), type some notes, and move on. I can easily imagine most nursing tasks being subsumed by robotics.

The same goes for brewers, soldiers, cops, and teachers. Soldier, cop, and teacher robots are already being tested, or actually deployed…and it’s early yet. If a safe, highly dense source of power is developed, that will vastly accelerate the process. At best, there will be far fewer humans involved, monitoring the robots, much as software engineers are now monitoring the agentic AIs.

I’m not sure how human society will adapt. The optimistic view (championed by Elon Musk) is that we’re headed for a “Star Trek economy” of essentially endless abundance for everyone. I hope things play out somewhere along those lines…

I’ve personally been impacted very heavily by LLM technology. Two of my major skills, coding and writing, have been greatly devalued by it. I’m relying on one of the truly core human traits to compensate - adaptability. That’s an area where LLMs currently lag far behind.

We’ll see how things go from here… ;-)
children.textZhHtml:
我认为你没有考虑到机器人技术的快速进步。

几天前我在医院，思考着众多带着监视器和各种类型的设备在便携式护理站周围转来转去的护士。他们会在一个房间停下来，测量病人的血压（以及其他一些事情），写下一些笔记，然后继续前进。我可以很容易地想象大多数护理任务都被机器人所取代。

酿酒师、士兵、警察和教师也是如此。士兵、警察和教师机器人已经在测试或实际部署……而且还为时过早。如果开发出一种安全、高密度的能源，那将大大加速这一进程。充其量，参与监控机器人的人员将会少得多，就像软件工程师现在监控代理人工智能一样。

我不确定人类社会将如何适应。乐观的观点（由埃隆·马斯克倡导）是，我们正在走向一种“星际迷航经济”，为每个人带来本质上无尽的富足。我希望事情能沿着这些方向发展……

我个人受到法学硕士技术的影响很大。我的两项主要技能，编码和写作，已经被它大大贬值了。我依靠人类真正核心的特质之一来弥补——适应性。这是法学硕士目前远远落后的领域。

我们将看看事情如何发展……;-)

children.author: kaffekaka
children.textRawHtml:
> I can easily imagine most nursing tasks being subsumed by robotics

I think you are greatly underestimating the difficulty of automating nursing tasks.

About teachers: some amount teaching profession can be automated, but the parts that cannot (in any reasonable way in the foreseeable future) are perhaps the most core aspects of teaching.
children.textZhHtml:
> 我可以很容易地想象大多数护理任务都被机器人技术所涵盖

我认为你大大低估了自动化护理任务的难度。

关于教师：一些教学职业可以自动化，但不能（在可预见的未来以任何合理的方式）的部分可能是教学的最核心方面。

children.author: Recurecur
children.textRawHtml:
We shall see about how much of nursing can be automated. I do think that the human presence of a nurse (particularly if of the opposite sex to the patient) is helpful. That could still be provided on a less frequent basis.

As to the rest of their function, I think probably the biggest obstacle will be the ability to safely manipulate the human body, as in turning or moving the patient. That requires delicacy, advanced tactile sensors, and physical power. For fine detail work, such as finding a vein with a needle, the technology already exists. Elon Musk also predicts that robotic surgery will rapidly outpace human surgeons, and I agree there.

On the subject of human teachers, my comment is similar to that about human nurses. A human connection helps with motivation. That said, I think video serves much the same function, and with video one teacher can reach an unlimited number of classrooms. That’s independent of how humanistic the teaching robots will become, and I expect that will also improve rapidly. We are nearing singularity like situations with engineering problems, in other words recursive improvement without much if any human intervention.
children.textZhHtml:
我们将了解有多少护理可以实现自动化。我确实认为护士在场（尤其是与患者异性的护士）是有帮助的。这仍然可以以较低的频率提供。

至于它们的其余功能，我认为最大的障碍可能是安全操纵人体的能力，例如转动或移动患者。这需要精致、先进的触觉传感器和体力。对于精细工作，例如用针寻找静脉，该技术已经存在。埃隆·马斯克还预测机器人手术将迅速超过人类外科医生，我对此表示同意。

关于人类教师的问题，我的评论与人类护士的评论类似。人际关系有助于激励。也就是说，我认为视频具有大致相同的功能，通过视频，一名教师可以覆盖无限数量的教室。这与教学机器人的人性化程度无关，我预计这也会迅速改善。我们正接近工程问题的奇点，换句话说，无需太多人为干预即可实现递归改进。

children.author: buddhistdude
children.textRawHtml: What does it matter how difficult it is? That only means it's gonna take a while longer.
children.textZhHtml: 难度有多大又有什么关系呢？这仅意味着需要更长的时间。

children.author: rayiner
children.textRawHtml:
That’s not how technology works. We went from first flight in 1903 to a man on the moon in 1969. Then we basically did almost nothing in aerospace for the next 50 years. We never got past the supersonic barrier for feasible commercial air travel. Apart from somewhat worse fuel efficiency, a 747 from 1969 can achieve basically the same trips in the same amount of time as a 787 or A350.

What looks like exponential curves turn into S-shaped curves everywhere. In the last century, coal power plants have gotten less than twice as efficient. A professor at law school was giving a lecture on technological singularity back in 2011. And I pointed out that Moore’s law was already dead. And in fact in the decade since then improvements came far slower than they did from 1990-2000.
children.textZhHtml:
技术不是这样运作的。从1903年首次飞行到1969年载人登月。接下来的50年里，我们在航空航天领域几乎没有做任何事情。我们从未突破过可行的商业航空旅行的超音速障碍。除了燃油效率稍差之外，1969 年生产的 747 可以在相同的时间内实现与 787 或 A350 基本相同的行程。

看起来指数曲线到处都变成了 S 形曲线。在上个世纪，燃煤电厂的效率还不到两倍。早在 2011 年，法学院的一位教授就技术奇点做了一次演讲。我指出摩尔定律已经失效了。事实上，此后的十年里，进步的速度比 1990 年至 2000 年要慢得多。

children.author: somenameforme
children.textRawHtml: When things are spread out over time people are able to adjust to the point that society, as a whole, might not even notice there was a problem, even if for some segment of that society it might feel like the end of the world - or at least an incomparable inflection point. The only real problem you have is when things come on hard and fast, like a tsunami.
children.textZhHtml: 当事情随着时间的推移而分散时，人们能够适应到整个社会甚至可能没有注意到存在问题的程度，即使对于社会的某些部分来说，这可能感觉像是世界末日 - 或者至少是一个无与伦比的拐点。你遇到的唯一真正的问题是当事情突然来临时，就像海啸一样。

stories.title: AMD acquires Taalas to boost inference performance by etching models in silicon
stories.titleZh: AMD 收购 Taalas，通过在硅中蚀刻模型来提高推理性能

comments.author: TechTechTech
comments.textRawHtml:
I think what will happen is what happened to something like 4K video decoding before where it ends up in silicon costing almost nothing to run extremely fast on device.

"Good enough" LLM functionality (for the use case) will be on-die or on-chip for cars, appliances, etc. This will provide speeds of chatjimmy at a battery-level power consumption.

Probably this will also happen for software engineering. Some usb-powered AI accelerator with Kimi K3 (and in future even better) performance running at 10K+ tokens/sec under 50W of power purchasable for almost no cost. Need a better model? Buy the new hardware. Old hardware is probably still fine for a lot of other use-cases. I expect China to be a big player here, it fits their open-model and hardware-manufacturing strategy.
comments.textZhHtml:
我认为将会发生的情况与之前 4K 视频解码之类的事情一样，它最终会在芯片上几乎不需要花费任何成本就可以在设备上运行得极快。

“足够好”的 LLM 功能（针对用例）将位于汽车、电器等的芯片上或芯片上。这将以电池级功耗提供 chatjimmy 的速度。

这可能也会发生在软件工程中。一些 USB 供电的 AI 加速器具有 Kimi K3（将来甚至更好）的性能，在 50W 功率下以 10K+ 代币/秒的速度运行，几乎可以免费购买。需要更好的模型吗？购买新硬件。旧硬件可能仍然适用于许多其他用例。我预计中国将成为这里的重要参与者，这符合他们的开放模式和硬件制造战略。

children.author: mixermachine
children.textRawHtml:
Scaling a model on a chip is quite hard. ChatJimmy is based on Llama 3.1 8 billion. Kimi K3 has 2.8 trillion parameters. That are 350x more parameters.

I would expect that Gemma 4 E2B (approx 5.1 billion parameters) or maybe even Gemma 4 26 billion A4B at some point is running on a chip.
children.textZhHtml:
在芯片上扩展模型非常困难。 ChatJimmy 基于 Llama 3.1 8 亿。 Kimi K3有2.8万亿个参数。 参数数量增加了 350 倍。

我预计 Gemma 4 E2B（大约 51 亿个参数）甚至 Gemma 4 260 亿个 A4B 在某个时刻都在芯片上运行。

children.author: Closi
children.textRawHtml:
Scaling is definetly hard - but there is no absolute requirement to put huge flagship models into this technology (although it might be possible over time).

A fairly dumb but FAST model has it's own totally distinct use-cases even if it can't be scaled in size. Think about a LLM-infused-Alexa where the response time is instant. Where you can request it looks at hotel options in Montreal, and it starts answering in half a second rather than a few minutes.

Plus some sort of slow smart + fast dumb combo architectures might also work really well for different classes of problems.
children.textZhHtml:
扩展确实很困难 - 但没有绝对要求将大型旗舰模型放入这项技术中（尽管随着时间的推移可能会实现）。

一个相当愚蠢但快速的模型有它自己完全不同的用例，即使它无法扩展大小。想想一个注入法学硕士的 Alexa，它的响应时间是即时的。您可以在其中请求它查看蒙特利尔的酒店选择，它会在半秒而不是几分钟内开始回答。

加上某种慢速智能+快速愚蠢的组合架构也可能非常适合不同类别的问题。

children.author: paulryanrogers
children.textRawHtml:
> Where you can request it looks at hotel options in Montreal, and it starts answering in half a second

Yet the answers will get outdated quickly whilst the silicon is fixed.

然而，当芯片修复时，答案很快就会过时。

children.author: jermaustin1
children.textRawHtml:
I have found that for some personal prose-related projects, QWEN 3.6 35B A3B is an amazing model even quantized down to 4 bits. I actually find it's "writing" style as a GM for an LLM-powered solo text adventure game, better than even some of the faster/dummer frontier models like GPT-5.6-Luna or Haiku 4.5, and it runs (slowly) on a 3090 with a 80k context.

So I have faith in these embedded LLM chips when it comes to fun projects like that. I have not personally found my quantized QWEN good at agentic tasks, though, and it LOVES to make shit up when asking questions about documents in the prompt.
children.textZhHtml:
我发现对于一些个人散文相关的项目，QWEN 3.6 35B A3B 是一个令人惊叹的模型，甚至量化到 4 位。实际上，我发现它是作为 LLM 支持的单人文本冒险游戏的 GM 的“编写”风格，甚至比一些更快/更笨的前沿模型（如 GPT-5.6-Luna 或 Haiku 4.5）更好，并且它在具有 80k 上下文的 3090 上运行（缓慢）。

因此，当涉及到此类有趣的项目时，我对这些嵌入式 LLM 芯片充满信心。不过，我个人并没有发现我的量化 QWEN 擅长代理任务，而且它喜欢在提示中询问有关文档的问题时胡编乱造。

children.author: dpedu
children.textRawHtml: 350x is only about 10-20 years of improvement, using CPU FLOPS as the benchmark.

Haven't CPUs largely plateaued? They're just getting bigger, more power hungry, and multiplying cores.

children.textZhHtml:
CPU 还没有基本稳定下来吗？它们只是变得越来越大，更加耗电，并且核心数量不断增加。

children.textZhHtml: 据我所知，这些不一定是 CPU。 ASICS 非常适合此目的。这将是运行法学硕士的最具成本效益的方式。

children.author: formerly_proven
children.textRawHtml: It's quite telling that the 8B Taalas chip was already reticle-sized on TSMC N6. I mean, we're talking about a process that does ~100 MTr/mm², ROM needs about one transistor per bit, but can probably be packed more densely than general logic. Something like, say, 150 megabit/mm² is not a lot. N6 has a 850 mm² reticle limit. This roughly tracks, the article says the chip has 8B parameters and apparently spends about half the area on ROM. There's a reason AI accelerators just use a ton of silicon area (each HBM3 die is >1000mm² of silicon). I imagine this is not terribly viable unless they make it a lot more space efficient e.g. using MLC ROM if they don't already, or use stacked dies with a ROM-optimized process. And then we're back to not cheap, though reticle chips were never in the cheap area to begin with.
children.textZhHtml: 很明显，8B Taalas 芯片在台积电 N6 上已经达到了十字线大小。我的意思是，我们正在讨论的流程约为 100 MTr/mm²，ROM 每位大约需要一个晶体管，但可能可以比一般逻辑封装得更密集。比如说，150 兆位/平方毫米并不是很多。 N6 的十字线限制为 850 mm²。这大致跟踪，文章称该芯片有 8B 参数，并且显然在 ROM 上花费了大约一半的面积。 AI 加速器仅使用大量硅面积（每个 HBM3 芯片的硅面积 >1000mm²）是有原因的。我认为这不是非常可行，除非它们能够提高空间效率，例如使用 MLC ROM（如果尚未使用），或者使用具有 ROM 优化流程的堆叠芯片。然后我们又回到了不便宜的情况，尽管掩模版芯片一开始就不是便宜的区域。

children.author: Tuna-Fish
children.textRawHtml:
Taalas exploits the low cardinality to store one 4-bit weight with one transistor. (They are using metal layer traces for the ROM, and connecting an access transistor to light up one of 16 options.)

Their system is honestly very efficient for the weights, the problem is the KV-cache. That's why HC1 only supports such short context, they use SRAM for that and spend most of what's left of the die for it. The recent advancements that made attention more efficient are probably going to be very useful for them.
children.textZhHtml:
Taalas 利用低基数用一个晶体管存储一个 4 位权重。 （他们为 ROM 使用金属层走线，并连接一个存取晶体管来点亮 16 个选项之一。）

他们的系统对于权重来说确实非常高效，问题在于 KV 缓存。这就是为什么 HC1 只支持如此短的上下文，他们为此使用 SRAM，并为此花费了芯片剩余的大部分内容。最近提高注意力效率的进步可能对他们非常有用。

They make many bold promises, but their core goal is neatly encapsulated on the website:

"Imagine a future where a handful of people can conduct scientific research and engineering tasks much more rapidly, and with higher quality, than massive teams of scientists and engineers do today."

This is the same goal as every other AI company out there. Automate away the human employees and let a small number of "people" (note that they do not say scientists or engineers for this part) take the credit and financial rewards for every good thing this human-free system produces.

children.author: tern
children.textRawHtml:
I love this question. If history is a guide, some version of that is what will happen (employment doesn't seem to go down, despite technological progress and population + economic growth).

I suspect the root cause is that it's harder and scarier to imagine good outcomes. It exposes us to disappointment, and when you do it publicly, it looks "crazy".

Another explanation is that there's no direct consumer for "more." Individuals, corporations and states are not in themselves interested in "a larger amount of science," or anything analogous, despite the fact that they would all benefit ambiently.

The net effect is that it's only "safe" to claim reduced risk (i.e. lower costs).
children.textZhHtml:
我喜欢这个问题。如果以史为鉴，那么的某些版本就是将会发生的情况（尽管技术进步和人口+经济增长，就业似乎并没有下降）。

我怀疑根本原因是想象好的结果更加困难和可怕。它让我们感到失望，而当你公开这样做时，它看起来“疯狂”。

另一种解释是，没有直接的消费者需要“更多”。个人、企业和国家本身并不对“大量的科学”或任何类似的东西感兴趣，尽管事实上他们都会从环境中受益。

最终的结果是，只有声称降低风险（即降低成本）才是“安全”的。

comments.author: hellojomp
comments.textRawHtml:
On the topic of taste, I think of this quote in Susan Sontag's "Notes On 'Camp'" often:

“For taste governs every free — as opposed to rote — human response. Nothing is more decisive. There is taste in people, visual taste, taste in emotion — and there is taste in acts, taste in morality. Intelligence, as well, is really a kind of taste: taste in ideas. (One of the facts to be reckoned with is that taste tends to develop very unevenly. It's rare that the same person has good visual taste and good taste in people and taste in ideas.)

Taste has no system and no proofs. But there is something like a logic of taste: the consistent sensibility which underlies and gives rise to a certain taste. A sensibility is almost, but not quite, ineffable. Any sensibility which can be crammed into the mold of a system, or handled with the rough tools of proof, is no longer a sensibility at all. It has hardened into an idea..."
comments.textZhHtml:
说到品味这个话题，我经常想起苏珊·桑塔格的《坎普笔记》中的这句话：

“因为品味支配着每一个自由的——而不是死记硬背的——人类的反应。没有什么比这更具有决定性的了。人有品味，视觉品味，情感品味——行为有品味，道德有品味。智力实际上也是一种品味：思想中的品味。（必须考虑的事实之一）品味往往发展得非常不平衡。）

品味没有系统，也没有证据：支撑并产生某种品味的一致的情感几乎是不可言喻的，但并非完全是不可言喻的。它不再是一种情感，而是一种想法……”

children.author: ulrikrasmussen
children.textRawHtml:
An important feature of taste is also that it is highly variable between people, and because there is no system or proof of good taste, we cannot really say that one person's taste is objectively better than another's. This is what causes one person to build a large software system in a classical OOP language while another builds almost the same system in a typed functional language, each following their own internal logic of what is good taste. In the end we learn something from it, and maybe someone who worked on both projects refine their taste and starts preferring something that lies in between the two paradigms and comes up with a new interesting programming language.

One thing I fear is going to happen when more and more people use LLM's for coding is that they will default to the "average taste" of the LLM, and we will stop getting new interesting ideas about how to build things.
children.textZhHtml:
品味的一个重要特征还在于它在人与人之间存在很大差异，而且由于没有良好品味的系统或证据，我们不能真正说一个人的品味客观上优于另一个人。这就是为什么一个人用经典的 OOP 语言构建一个大型软件系统，而另一个人用类型化函数语言构建几乎相同的系统，每个人都遵循自己的内部逻辑，即什么是好品味。最后我们从中学到了一些东西，也许从事这两个项目的人会改进他们的品味，并开始更喜欢介于两种范式之间的东西，并提出一种新的有趣的编程语言。

当越来越多的人使用 LLM 进行编码时，我担心会发生的一件事是，他们将默认为 LLM 的“平均品味”，而我们将不再获得关于如何构建东西的新的有趣想法。

children.author: ben_w
children.textRawHtml:
> One thing I fear is going to happen when more and more people use LLM's for coding is that they will default to the "average taste" of the LLM, and we will stop getting new interesting ideas about how to build things.

I don't think it will have any impact at all on creativity in coding.

Creativity is rewarded in humans, just not by their employment where both training examples and monetary rewards can be found, rather the creativity is rewarded by challenges such as code golf, demoscene, and so on.

comments.author: jerf
comments.textRawHtml:
This is a really important concept for developers.

One aspect for developers that I see quite often is the assertion that "We can't have X without giving up more Y", most commonly "we can't have more security without giving up on user experience". With the Pareto idea in mind, we can see that that statement is true, if and only if you are in fact on the Pareto frontier of security and user experience already.

However, many times these confident pronouncements are being made when the system under question is quite evidently not on the Pareto frontier in the first place and indeed you can get more of one without giving up the other.

Making it more tricky is that in business, you can never discard "money" as a dimension, so unless you're taking "money" as one of the dimensions in the original comparison you want to do, it sneaks its way in. Or, a composite time/money, or "cost to business", or some other similar concept, time & money aren't orthogonal and don't need to be treated as two separate dimensions in general, though you can if you want. Which puts you into the 3D case, and as the page says, that grows the frontier quite a lot, which is good in some ways and bad in others. Nevertheless, in my opinion it is still often the case that even in that space we are often making "tradeoffs" without checking that we're on the Pareto frontier in the first place.
comments.textZhHtml:
这对于开发人员来说是一个非常重要的概念。

对于开发人员来说，我经常看到的一个方面是这样的断言：“我们不能在不放弃更多 Y 的情况下拥有 X”，最常见的是“如果不放弃用户体验，我们就不能拥有更多的安全性”。考虑到帕累托思想，我们可以看到，这个说法是正确的，当且仅当您实际上已经处于安全和用户体验的帕累托前沿。

但是，很多时候，当所讨论的系统显然一开始就不在帕累托前沿，并且实际上您可以在不放弃另一个的情况下获得更多时，就会做出这些自信的声明。

更棘手的是，在商业中，您永远不能放弃“金钱”作为一个维度，因此除非您将“金钱”作为您想要进行的原始比较中的维度之一，否则它会悄悄进入。或者，时间/金钱的复合，或“业务成本”，或其他一些类似的概念，时间和金钱不是正交的，通常不需要被视为两个单独的维度，尽管如果您愿意，也可以这样做。这会让你进入 3D 情况，正如页面上所说，这使边界增长了很多，这在某些方面是好的，但在其他方面却是坏的。尽管如此，在我看来，即使在这个空间中，我们仍然经常进行“权衡”，而没有首先检查我们是否处于帕累托边界。

Any technological and societal progress is going to have negative consequences. stories.title: New Mexico court orders Meta to pay $567m over harms to children’s mental health

comments.author: tmp10423288442
comments.textRawHtml:
A lot of people on this story are making the usual snarky remarks that, oh, this is just a slap on the wrist—some trivial proportion of Meta’s global revenue. And that is true, but unlike the EU, for example, New Mexico is a tiny jurisdiction. It only has a little bit more than 2 million people.

So actually, a fine—or a judgment—of $942 million that applies just to New Mexico is enormous. If you look at Meta’s revenue from the U.S. and Canada and assign it proportionally by population, you find that Meta only earned about $1.5 billion to $2 billion total from New Mexico over the past five years. The exact figure depends on whether you allocate purely by population or account for purchasing power, which makes the estimate a little lower because New Mexico is a poorer state than the U.S. average.

Given that, the judgment is a half to two-thirds of what Meta could have obtained from New Mexico. So it is actually a serious deterrent, assuming Meta thinks New Mexico would continue to impose fines of that size.

I also think that there’s a good chance this judgment gets overturned or significantly reduced on appeal, but even if the fine drops to half its current level, it would be proportionately larger than almost any fine against any company, let alone tech, that I’ve heard of.
comments.textZhHtml:
这篇报道中的很多人都发表了常见的尖刻评论，哦，这只是小事一桩——占 Meta 全球收入的微不足道的一部分。确实如此，但与欧盟不同的是，新墨西哥州是一个很小的司法管辖区。它只有 200 万多一点点的人口。

所以实际上，仅适用于新墨西哥州的 9.42 亿美元罚款（或判决）是巨大的。如果你看看 Meta 在美国和加拿大的收入，并按人口比例分配，你会发现过去 5 年 Meta 从新墨西哥州总共只赚了约 15 亿到 20 亿美元。确切的数字取决于你是纯粹按人口分配还是考虑购买力，这使得估计值略低，因为新墨西哥州是一个比美国平均水平更贫穷的州。

鉴于此，该判断是 Meta 可以从新墨西哥州获得的一半到三分之二。因此，假设 Meta 认为新墨西哥州将继续征收如此数额的罚款，这实际上是一种严重的威慑。

我还认为，这一判决很有可能在上诉时被推翻或大幅减少，但即使罚款降至目前水平的一半，按比例来说，它也将比我听说过的几乎任何针对任何公司的罚款都要高，更不用说科技公司了。

children.author: tristanj
children.textRawHtml:
This analysis actually understates how massive and outsized the penalties are. The court ruling only applies to children in New Mexico under age 18.

New Mexico has ~450,000 people under age 18, of which roughly 140,000 are between ages 13-17 (Meta officially requires age 13+ to use their platforms). Recent Pew surveys of U.S. teens ages 13–17 show ~70% of teenagers use Instagram and ~30% use Facebook.

In New Mexico, Instagram and Facebook would have ~100,000 users in the 13-17 group. That's not everyone, some underage users may lie about their age, so add in ~30,000 unauthorized users under age 13. Overall, around 130,000 people in the affected class.

The judge assessed $942 million in total penalties, and dividing that $942 million across 130,000 users equals approximately $7,250 in fines per user.

If this fine remains, and Meta pays out to the affected parties, these kids could end up rewarded with thousands of dollars for just for having a Facebook or Instagram account. Which creates some bizarre incentives, minors get rewarded for signing up for the platforms that are harming them in the first place.

新墨西哥州约有 450,000 名 18 岁以下人口，其中约 140,000 人年龄在 13-17 岁之间（Meta 官方要求 13 岁以上才能使用其平台）。皮尤研究中心最近对 13-17 岁美国青少年进行的调查显示，约 70% 的青少年使用 Instagram，约 30% 使用 Facebook。

Monitoring server logs, continuous security audits and investigating every received exception now becomes possible.

I'm thinking about having it automatically filter and re-rank my social media feeds so I can steer the algorithm instead of the other way around.

I think you're overlooking the fact that for long-horizon tasks, even small errors compound over time and can lead to catastrophic outcomes.

For simple queries, we have reached the threshold since the beginning of the year, and models are good enough from every provider to make a meaningful difference between one another. (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, MuseSpark, Kimi, DeepSeek, GLM...)

The real unlock will be, and you can already see it with GPT-5.6 and Fable-5, to delegate complex enough tasks that will take more than 24 hours to get done and they will not lose track. I'm not talking about a loop, but the actual intelligence to recover from these compounding errors that accumulate in dumber models.

We're still a long way from the intelligence needed to let one of these agents go ahead and supervise multiple layers of sub-agents underneath to do complex orchestration. The future looks very promising and exciting. Imagine having the possibility of a Frontier model orchestrating as many sub-agents as needed that are running on cheaper models like DeepSeek.

stories.title: I'm switching my phone from Android to Linux
stories.titleZh: 我正在将手机从 Android 切换到 Linux

comments.author: reorder9695
comments.textRawHtml:
I've come to the conclusion that I actually really like Android as an operating system, the internals seem remarkably well thought out and ideal for the mobile use case (so long as you're running a userdebug build with the ability to adb root in when needed), most of people's issues aren't really with Android (although Google reducing the AOSP release schedule isn't a good sign).

I think the real problem is Google Play Services. It's far, far too tightly integrated in a way that it just seems like Android was designed to be unusable without. It's installed as a location manager internally, which gives it a shitload of permissions by default that you never grant it. There's absolutely no reason everything (notifications, the app store, some location services) has to be packaged together into one thing instead of each having its own module that can be removed at will. Play integrity just plain shouldn't exist and as far as I'm concerned is purely there to ensure no one creates a real play services alternative or another mobile OS with Android compatibility.

The ideal outcome for me would be keeping Android but effectively dissolving Play Services and instead having the concept of a core services, where instead of apps choosing to use Firebase for notifications, they instead bind to the system notifications service, and as the user I choose which implementation I want, preferably with it not installed as a system app. I'm well aware that's not going to happen, but it seems like the most practical way to break up the Google/Apple monopoly to me, Android's great but Google's services aren't.
comments.textZhHtml:
我得出的结论是，我实际上非常喜欢 Android 作为操作系统，其内部结构似乎经过深思熟虑，非常适合移动用例（只要您运行的是 userdebug 版本，并且能够在需要时进行 adb root），大多数人的问题实际上与 Android 无关（尽管 Google 缩短 AOSP 发布时间表并不是一个好兆头）。

我认为真正的问题是 Google Play 服务。它的集成太过紧密，以至于 Android 被设计为没有它就无法使用。它在内部作为位置管理器安装，默认情况下会给它大量的权限，而你永远不会授予它。绝对没有理由将所有内容（通知、应用程序商店、一些位置服务）打包在一起成为一个东西，而不是每个东西都有自己的可以随意删除的模块。游戏完整性根本不应该存在，就我而言，纯粹是为了确保没有人创建真正的游戏服务替代方案或另一个具有 Android 兼容性的移动操作系统。

对我来说，理想的结果是保留 Android，但有效地溶解 Play 服务，并采用核心服务的概念，其中应用程序不选择使用 Firebase 进行通知，而是绑定到系统通知服务，并且作为用户，我选择我想要的实现，最好不将其安装为系统应用程序。我很清楚这不会发生，但对我来说，这似乎是打破 Google/Apple 垄断的最实际方法，Android 很棒，但 Google 的服务却不是。

children.author: rickdeckard
children.textRawHtml:
> I think the real problem is Google Play Services. It's far, far too tightly integrated in a way that it just seems like Android was designed to be unusable without.

This is somehow by intention. In the ramp-up of Android adoption, Vendors and carriers started to fork Android and deviate too much from the core. Google needed a leverage to tie them to stay compatible to the ecosystem, Google Mobile Services (GMS) was the tool to do so. "Pass the compatibility test suite and you qualify to preload GMS".

Then, at some point, Google implemented API's in the OS which call Google's cloud infrastructure (e.g. Location services), which they didn't want to commit to the Android source for the risk of them being forked and modified, so they started to implement them in a precompiled "Google Play Services" module.

Over time, it seems Google Play Services became the preferred vehicle for Google to rollout any kind of API-changes to have them applied on all devices immediately, without waiting for the vendor to do an OS-Upgrade.

The result is that Google now promotes Google Play Service API's as the way for the most widely compatible implementation of an app. Which is...not wrong, but in the larger picture also the reason why Android is not considered "real" open-source (anymore).

You are missing a few steps there.

First came Project Treble, where Android was refactored to actually have a stable ABI for drivers, by pretending Linux is a microkernel, all drivers run in userspace, use Android IPC to talk with the kernel, and are implemented in a mix of C++, Java and more recently Rust.

Since Android 8, traditional Linux kernel drivers are considered legacy.

https://source.android.com/docs/core/architecture/hal

However adoption by OEMs was still not enforced, because "our partners freedom" kind of thing,

So Project Mainline come to be, where Android was further modularised and userspace components could be updated via PlayStore.

https://source.android.com/docs/core/ota/modular-system

With, as already mentioned by others, APEX as delivery format,

https://source.android.com/docs/core/ota/apex

Naturally all of this only works via PlayStore services, and is related to the "Google Play System Update", or similar, that you can find in the settings section.

I think you are in the minority of people that feel Android is a well built "OS". Maybe from an end-user point of view it "does what you want" but its underlying architecture I think is pretty poor.

I have spent the past 2 years off and on modifying AOSP (for "reasons") and I am constantly amazed the poor quality of the code base and badly architected the overall system is.

It's a bunch of re-inventions of the wheel (start-up daemon manager, IPC, HAL, GUI, etc) with the "upper layers" written in Java with a mix of C/C++. Mixing the metaphor of a Java "run time environment" with a Linux-based kernel results in a hodepodge of pieces and having seen it up close it makes sense why "Android" user experience varies so much device to device.

Did Android need it's own bastardized libc for example (bionic)? Did Android need to have it's own start-up daemon manager? A "HAL" in C++ (wrapping Linux kernel capability) with a bunch of bridges to Java via JNI?

Writing an application for Android is also a byztantine mess of NDK, SDKs, Java build systems (Maven, Gradle, etc), XML files, Java, Kotlin, etc. Why can't icons just be SVGs, why do these have to be in some XML-formatted resource? The list goes on.

I think it was one of those cases where "the road to hell was paved with good intentions".

I'm old enough and was very pro-android in the early days when it first released. I absolutely remember the frustrations around having vendors just REFUSE to update the OS on devices. Even things that were brand spanking new often got left to rot, and the OS updates in those days were genuinely meaningful software updates - Lots of new capabilities.

So I was actually ok with Google going down the route of moving critical software into an installable package that they controlled, that would provide a way to get new capabilities onto devices that manufacturers didn't give a shit about anymore.

But the problem is that "Google" today sure as hell isn't the google that I liked back then (and even that google was starting to shift tone).

I still strongly believe that the appropriate regulation for this situation (across both iOS and Android) is that the company that makes the OS should be prohibited from running any sort of app store, and app stores must be selectable at device initialization (ex - the Internet Explorer ruling, but for app stores).
